source_text:
Οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἡμῖν εὐηγγελίσθησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξεπέμφθη.
ὁ Χριστος οὖν ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ: ἐγένοντο οὖν ἀμφότερα εὐτάκτως ἐκ θελήματος θεοῦ.
παραγγελίας οὖν λαβόντες καὶ πληροφορηθέντες διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ πιστωθέντες ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ θεοῦ, μετὰ πληροφορίας πνεύματος ἁγίου ἐξῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι, τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ μέλλειν ἔρχεσθαι,
κατὰ χώρας οὖν καὶ πόλεις κηρύσσοντες καθίστανον τὰς ἀπαρχὰς αὐτῶν, δοκιμάσαντες τῷ πνεύματι, εἰς ἐπισκόπους καὶ διακόνους τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν.
καὶ τοῦτο οὐ καινῶς: ἐκ γὰρ δὴ πολλῶν χρόνων ἐγέγραπτο περὶ ἐπισκόπων καὶ διακόνων. οὕτως γάρ που λέγει ἡ γραφή: Καταστήσω τοὺς ἐπισκόπους αὐτῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ τοὺς διακόνους αὐτῶν ἐν πίστει.
thought_title: The apostles' ordered mission from God through Christ
orientation: The author is arguing that God has established a fixed order of ministry, and now traces that order from God through Christ to the apostles and their appointed leaders.
pass_a_gloss: The apostles [were] evangelized to us from the Lord Jesus Christ, Jesus the Christ was sent out from God. The Christ therefore [was] from God and the apostles [were] from the Christ: both things therefore happened in an orderly way from [the] will of God. Therefore having received commands and having been fully assured through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ and having been made faithful in the word of God, with full assurance of [the] Holy Spirit they went out preaching the good news, [that] the kingdom of God [was] about to come. Therefore according to regions and cities preaching they appointed the firstfruits of them, having tested [them] by the Spirit, as bishops and deacons of those about to believe. And this [was] not newly: for indeed from many times it had been written about bishops and deacons. For thus somewhere says the scripture: I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith.

lemmas.gloss: were evangelized, received the good news

choices.why: The passive of εὐαγγελίζω means the apostles were the recipients of the gospel message from Christ; 'were evangelized' is awkward in English, so a passive construction that keeps the sense of receiving is clearer.
The verb means to be fully convinced or assured; the passive participle keeps the sense that this assurance came to them through the resurrection.
The passive of πιστόω means to be made trustworthy or confirmed in faith; the passive voice is important because God is the implied agent.
The term refers to the first converts in each place, offered as the first portion of the harvest; keeping the agricultural metaphor preserves the source's imagery.

choices.english: having tested them by the Spirit
choices.why: The dative τῷ πνεύματι indicates the means or instrument of testing; 'by the Spirit' keeps the instrumental force clear.
The adverb καινῶς means 'in a new way' or 'as something new'; rendering it as 'not as a novelty' captures the point that this practice was not an innovation.

bible_refs.note: Καταστήσω τοὺς ἐπισκόπους αὐτῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ τοὺς διακόνους αὐτῶν ἐν πίστει

pass_b_english: The apostles received the good news for us from the Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus the Christ was sent out from God.
So Christ came from God, and the apostles came from Christ. Both things happened in an orderly way, according to God's will.

After they received their commands and were fully assured through the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, and after they were made faithful in the word of God, they went out with the full assurance of the Holy Spirit, proclaiming the good news that the kingdom of God was about to come.
As they preached through the regions and cities, they tested their firstfruits by the Spirit and appointed them as bishops and deacons for those who were about to believe.
This was not a new practice. Long ago it had been written about bishops and deacons, for the scripture says somewhere: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith."

problems.quote: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith" (Isaiah 60:17).
problems.source_quote: Καταστήσω τοὺς ἐπισκόπους αὐτῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ τοὺς διακόνους αὐτῶν ἐν πίστει.
problems.why: The quoted verse does not appear in Isaiah 60:17; the citation is incorrect.
problems.fix: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith" (citation corrected or omitted).

edits.old: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith" (Isaiah 60:17).
edits.new: "I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith."

fixed: Removed the incorrect citation (Isaiah 60:17) from the quotation, since the source does not identify the passage and the cited verse does not contain these words.

problems.quote: The apostles received the good news for us from the Lord Jesus Christ
problems.source_quote: Οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἡμῖν εὐηγγελίσθησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
problems.why: Greek says the apostles proclaimed (were the agents of) the good news to us; English reverses agency making them receivers.
problems.fix: The apostles proclaimed the good news to us from the Lord Jesus Christ
problems.ruling: εὐηγγελίσθησαν is passive 'were evangelized to us' = apostles preached to us; English 'received' reverses agency.

edits.old: The apostles received the good news for us from the Lord Jesus Christ
edits.new: The apostles proclaimed the good news to us from the Lord Jesus Christ

fixed: The agency problem was real: the Greek has the apostles as the ones who proclaimed the good news to us, not as receivers. Fixed by changing 'received the good news for us' to 'proclaimed the good news to us'.

problems.quote: The apostles proclaimed the good news to us from the Lord Jesus Christ
problems.source_quote: Οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἡμῖν εὐηγγελίσθησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
problems.why: Greek uses passive εὐηγγελίσθησαν, meaning the apostles were proclaimed to us, not that they proclaimed.
problems.fix: The apostles were proclaimed to us by the Lord Jesus Christ, and Jesus the Christ was sent out from God.
problems.ruling: εὐηγγελίσθησαν is passive: 'were gospel-preached to us,' not active 'proclaimed.' The passive voice changes the meaning.

edits.old: The apostles proclaimed the good news to us from the Lord Jesus Christ
edits.new: The apostles were proclaimed to us by the Lord Jesus Christ

fixed: The agency problem is real: the Greek passive εὐηγγελίσθησαν means the apostles were proclaimed to us, not that they proclaimed. The edit changes the English to reflect the passive voice.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence so the apostles are clearly the recipients of the good news from Christ, and Christ is clearly the one sent from God; kept every claim and quotation intact while smoothing the flow for modern readers.

last_rejected.quote: and after they were made faithful in the word of God
last_rejected.source_quote: πιστωθέντες ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ θεοῦ
last_rejected.why: πιστόω means 'assured/confirmed', not 'made faithful'. Parallel to 'fully assured' earlier.
last_rejected.fix: and after they were confirmed in the word of God
last_rejected.ruling: πιστωθέντες = aorist passive participle of πιστόω, meaning ‘made faithful/confirmed’; translation “made faithful” is acceptable.
